purpose: Hand-maintained sign-off on every decision flip between the iteration-19 rules (commit 8a2050d) and the iteration-20 rules. scripts/check_routing_reachability.py joins this onto the generated flip table and FAILS on any flip that is not reviewed here, on any entry that no longer corresponds to a flip, and on any verdict of REJECT. A flip count on its own is not a review; this file is the review.

verdicts.ACCEPT: the new route is better for this task, not merely consistent with the new rule
verdicts.REJECT: the new route is worse -- fix the rule or the label, do not record the flip
verdicts.UNCERTAIN: defensible either way; recorded so it is re-read next time the rule moves

how_the_rule_column_is_produced: Not by hand. scripts/check_routing_reachability.py switches exactly one iteration-20 delta (tier, notch, e4, gates, badge) off at a time and reports which one restores the old route, so the attribution cannot rot when a rule changes.
headline: 91 of 154 corpus prompts flip. 82 involve the Terra -> Sol tier merge, 22 the retired notch (the two overlap), 6 the retired Astra gates, 2 E4. The badge histogram moves from Claude 122 / Codex 28 / none 4 to Claude 43 / Codex 107 / none 4. Against GPT-6.1 Sol no agentic-code, terminal-tool, deep-reasoning, long-context, research-synthesis, doc-data-understanding or computer-use row licenses a Claude DIRECTION under BD1, so at R<=2 those fall to efficiency and efficiency favours Sol; at R=3 a single-row lean still decides (BD1's R=3 clause), which is why the high-risk architecture prompts stay on Claude. The lean is large and it is recorded here so it is re-read, not because anyone found it wrong.
